- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **18** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a19b2a7a51d15b506cc916798bd5ac8788723288` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh

git fetch origin b18aa84d838230117772a2538cda6b3a66eaadf0 && git checkout b18aa84d838230117772a2538cda6b3a66eaadf0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a19b2a7a51d15b506cc916798bd5ac8788723288 1e4146df8ad2ed24f2d011b3b03842c2840a7dbe && git checkout -B drift-repro a19b2a7a51d15b506cc916798bd5ac8788723288 && git merge --no-ff 1e4146df8ad2ed24f2d011b3b03842c2840a7dbe

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a19b2a7a51d15b506cc916798bd5ac8788723288
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed

> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a19b2a7a51d15b506cc916798bd5ac8788723288` → pass the list as

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `1e4146df8ad2ed24f2d011b3b03842c2840a7dbe`
Local-runs: none

Owed by the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` declaration of claim `6238919385` alone. The diff touches no `packages/spec/src/**` file and no governed path. Read at 2026-10-17T20:26Z:
- the diff, the card and its thread, ruling `6232069920` as the card quotes it, and #24165's landed contract (`auth-service.ts` on `main`);
- the published `@better-auth/oauth-provider@1.7.3` `dist` (the lockfile pin), read and not run;
- this head's check-runs.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`AuthManager.verifyMcpAccessToken`'s result gains `organizationId?: string`: a widening, and correct.** `plugin-auth/src/index.ts` re-exports `./auth-manager.js` whole, so the method's type is published. The member is optional, so every caller compiles unchanged. It matches `IAuthService.verifyMcpAccessToken`'s result as #24165 widened it (contract review PASS `6237222227`). The dev measured the built `dist/index.d.ts` / `.d.mts` BASE `a237d7f496` vs head: exactly one declaration line is added. `platform-objects`' built declarations are byte-identical.
- **The issued MCP access token gains the claim `organization_id`.** The name is the contract's. It is not in the provider's `RESERVED_ACCESS_TOKEN_CLAIMS` set (`dist/introspect-*.mjs`), so it is not stripped at issuance.
  - Its only producer is `customAccessTokenClaims({ referenceId })`, and the reference comes only from `postLogin.consentReferenceId`.
  - The provider calls that hook with `{ user, session, scopes }` and nothing else (`dist/authorize-*.mjs`), so no request parameter reaches it. This is pinned: organization-looking authorize parameters change nothing recorded.
  - A consent with no active organization binds none, and its tokens carry no claim. No default value exists.
- **Existing consents re-confirm once.** The provider's consent lookup filters on `referenceId` whenever the hook answers one, so a null-reference consent does not satisfy an authorize made in an organization. This is pinned: a re-prompt once, none after, and an old refresh family that stays unbound. There is no dual path and no fallback, as the ruling requires.
- **The verifier refuses a present-but-malformed `organization_id`.** This narrows the verifier's acceptance for a shape this server never mints. The one path that can produce it is an administrator-written `sys_oauth_resource.custom_claims`, which the provider ranks above `customAccessTokenClaims`. This is a runtime behaviour of an existing fail-closed method, not a published accept set. Reading the claim as absent would be consumer-side leniency that masks the misconfiguration. Pinned with a control (the string case is accepted). Correct.
- **`reference_id` on `sys_oauth_consent`, `sys_oauth_refresh_token` and `sys_oauth_access_token` now names the bound organization.**
  - This is description prose only, with no field, type or schema change.
  - No stored row carries another meaning. The provider writes those columns only from `consentReferenceId`, which `plugin-auth` did not pass before (measured `null` on `main` by #24137's dev).
  - `sys_oauth_application.reference_id` is unchanged. The provider writes it only from `clientReference`, which is not passed.
- **No new config key or environment variable.** `postLogin` and `customAccessTokenClaims` are options of the provider instance. `shouldRedirect: () => false` adds no redirect: the provider reads `postLogin.page` only when `shouldRedirect` answers true.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-auth` `minor` (a published type widening and a new token claim) and `@objectstack/platform-objects` `patch` (description prose and the generated bundle rows). Both match the diff. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is at a line start in the PR body and in the changeset.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **The dev's flag, the malformed-claim refusal,** is judged in ① and holds.
- **The hand-translated `zh-CN` / `ja-JP` / `es-ES` leaves** follow AGENTS.md's `*.generated.ts` row. That is a convention, not a contract flag.
- **Two notes belong to the runtime read, not to this slice's contract.** They are carried to #24137:
  - A resource row's `customClaims` can replace the consent-bound organization. This is administrator configuration that the provider honours.
  - `vetOrganizationClaim` reads no membership under `single`.
- **Patch round 1 aligned two sentences with the contract's wording.** No membership guarantee is stated wider than `vetOrganizationClaim` gives.
- No open question was raised. No other flag.
